findings.body: The head commit records observed Mac stub runs but explicitly says no Windows result is claimed. The plan requires the functional check to record stubbed runs of both scripts. The Windows piped install, all-present path, and WSL2 guidance therefore still lack an observed outcome in the supplied evidence.
findings.title: Not done: functional check

findings.body: The Mac fixture always provides `git` and `node` here, and the Windows fixture does the same at `tests/test_sales_install.py:116`. No test makes either tool missing. Removing or breaking either script's Git or Node installer call would leave this test green, despite those being required laptop setup steps. Add missing-tool cases that assert the Homebrew and winget calls.
findings.title: Not done: test missing Git and Node installations

findings.body: Any directory with each browser prefix counts as installed, including an incomplete download or an old revision; Windows makes the same check at `scripts/install-windows.ps1:21`. Check mode can report nothing missing even when the project's tests cannot launch a browser. [Playwright requires browser binaries matched to its version](https://playwright.dev/docs/browsers).
findings.title: Check usable Playwright revisions before skipping installation

findings.body: A standalone `docker` command causes the Mac script to skip Docker Desktop; Windows uses the same command-only check at `scripts/install-windows.ps1:52`. The script can then say Docker is ready while there is no Desktop engine for prototype work. Check for a usable Desktop installation or give a plain instruction to start it. [Docker distinguishes the CLI from Desktop setup and startup](https://docs.docker.com/desktop/setup/install/mac-install/).
findings.title: Treat a Docker CLI without Docker Desktop as missing

findings.body: Done-when item 2 calls for running each script from a checklist one-liner. The task table assigns the checklist and README link to SPEC, and this branch has neither `docs/start-a-prototype.md` nor that README link. SPEC must publish the Mac `curl … | bash` and Windows `irm … | iex` commands to complete the user path.
findings.title: Later: SPEC — publish the checklist one-liners
